newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas called lower on weather, ample stocks.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas called lower on weather, ample stocks.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures were expected to open lower Friday, pressured by a weaker ACCESS session and next week's mild forecasts across most of the U.S., industry sources said.
February over-the-counter trade at 0940 EST ranged from about $2.70 to $2.73 per million British thermal units after settling at $2.794.
In ACCESS, February last traded 4.9 cents lower at $2.745.
Early cash indications at the Henry Hub were softer in the $2.77-2.85 per mmBtu range.

Although profit taking ahead of the weekend and the expiry on Monday may pressure the contract early, some traders expected the contract to rebound this afternoon, noting a rising open interest over the last few days.
Technically, traders said support in February was at the Dec 31 low of $2.613. Resistance was seen at $2.85, then $3.00, with better selling likely at $3.33, $3.64 and then $3.80-3.84.

In Thursday's cash market, Gulf Coast prices were five to 10 cents lower in the $2.90-2.95 area. Midcontinent prices lost about five cents to $2.80-2.85. New York city gate gas slipped five cents or more to about the $3.30 level.

Although temperatures in the Midwest are well below-normal and are expected to continue over the weekend, warmer air is forecast to return Monday and Tuesday. Mostly above-normal temperatures are also forecast for the Northeast by the middle of next week.
